chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Safwan from Sa'id al-A'raj from Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon them both)
Regarding a man who performed Dhihar with his wife and then fulfilled it, he said: 'There is nothing upon him.'

key_terms.ظَاهَرَ: Dhihar, an Islamic legal concept where a husband compares his wife to his mother's back, prohibiting sexual relations until expiation is made
key_terms.لَيْسَ عَلَيْهِ شَيْءٌ: There is nothing upon him (no further penalty or obligation)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a man who performs Dhihar and fulfills its expiation?
ai.summary: Transmitted through the chain of Musa ibn Ja'far (al-Kazim) in Shaykh al-Tusi's *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith clarifies that once the mandatory expiation (kaffarah) for Dhihar is fulfilled, the husband is absolved of any further legal penalty. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential view that the expiation serves as the complete rectification of the marital prohibition caused by the vow, restoring the wife's permissibility without additional conditions.
